results.claim: There is an explicit packing of 518 A10 rectangles in one A1 rectangle.
results.proof_sketch: Use container [0,594]×[0,841]. Place A_{i,j}=[37i,37(i+1)]×[26j,26(j+1)] for 0≤i<2, 0≤j<32 (64 rectangles). Place B_i=[74+37i,74+37(i+1)]×[0,26] for 0≤i<14 (14 rectangles). Finally place C_{i,j}=[74+26i,74+26(i+1)]×[26+37j,26+37(j+1)] for 0≤i<20, 0≤j<22 (440 rectangles). The three families occupy respectively [0,74]×[0,832], [74,592]×[0,26], and [74,594]×[26,840], so they are contained and have disjoint interiors. Their total size is 64+14+440=518.

results.claim: No packing can contain 519 A10 rectangles; a ten-residue periodic marker certificate gives the upper bound 518.
results.proof_sketch: By the source paper's integer-coordinate lemma, it suffices to consider integer placements. Mark unit cell (x,y) when (x mod 37,y mod 37) belongs to P={(3,3),(7,25),(10,14),(14,7),(18,29),(22,11),(25,33),(29,22),(33,36),(36,18)}. The sets of first and second coordinates are X={3,7,10,14,18,22,25,29,33,36} and Y={3,7,11,14,18,22,25,29,33,36}. In either cyclically ordered set, every four successive elements have first-to-fourth cyclic distance at least 11. Hence every block of 11 consecutive residues contains at most three elements, and every block of 26 residues contains at least seven. A 37×26 rectangle contains every x-residue once and 26 consecutive y-residues, so it contains at least seven marked cells; a 26×37 rectangle does likewise using X. In 594 columns, residues 0 and 1 occur 17 times and all others 16 times; every first coordinate in P therefore occurs 16 times. In 841 rows, residues 0,…,26 occur 23 times and residues 27,…,36 occur 22 times. Seven second coordinates of P are in the first group and three in the second, so the container has exactly 16(7·23+3·22)=3632 marked cells. Disjoint rectangles cover disjoint unit cells, hence 7n≤3632 and n≤⌊3632/7⌋=518.

final_writeup:
The recorded 258-versus-259 dichotomy is false for the literal ISO sizes supplied in the input. An A10 sheet is 26×37 mm and an A1 sheet is 594×841 mm; their exact orthogonal packing number is

OPT(594,841,37,26)=518.

A checkable lower-bound construction divides the container into three occupied blocks. The left block [0,74]×[0,832] is tiled by a 2×32 grid of 37×26 rectangles. The upper-right block [74,592]×[0,26] contains fourteen 37×26 rectangles. The lower-right block [74,594]×[26,840] is tiled by a 20×22 grid of 26×37 rectangles. These give 64+14+440=518 nonoverlapping sheets.

For the upper bound, use the ten residue pairs
P={(3,3),(7,25),(10,14),(14,7),(18,29),(22,11),(25,33),(29,22),(33,36),(36,18)} modulo 37, marking every unit cell with one of these residue pairs. Every 26-consecutive cyclic interval contains at least seven of the first-coordinate residues and at least seven of the second-coordinate residues. Consequently every integer-positioned A10 rectangle, in either orientation, contains at least seven marked cells. The entire A1 container contains exactly 3632 marked cells. Thus a packing of 519 sheets would require at least 7·519=3633 distinct marked cells, which is impossible. The source paper's integer-coordinate lemma extends this conclusion to placements initially having arbitrary real coordinates.

Therefore the maximum is 518, so neither 258 nor 259 is correct for A10-in-A1.
